slides.subtitle: Amsterdam, February 2027. The first Benelux CTO festival. Five hundred technical leaders, one day, and the night before it.

slides.title: Most technology events are not built for the people building it.

points.title: Built for the wrong room.
points.body: Conferences are programmed around chief executives, investors, and the people selling to them. Technical leaders end up in panels that perform.

points.title: Drowning in noise.
points.body: Recruiter spam, vendor pitches, surface-level debate. The signal that matters, how peers are actually shipping, never reaches the people who need it.

points.title: No shared frontier.
points.body: AI, regulation, infrastructure shifts, European technology sovereignty. The hardest questions of the next decade, and no forum built for them.

slides.title: A trusted room, two years in the making.

metrics.label: CTOs and VP Engineering in the network

slides.title: The room is worth being in because of what we do not sell.

points.title: No list, ever.
points.body: No attendee data leaves the building for cold outreach, and no mass mailing afterwards.

points.title: No pitch from the stage.
points.body: Partners send a senior technical voice rather than a sales lead.

points.title: Introductions, opt-in.
points.body: Connections happen in the room, and through matching people agree to.

slides.title: AI is leaving the browser. Robotics is leaving the lab. This is the room where they touch.

slides.title: Designed for depth, not for scale.

points.title: 09:00 · The film, then a keynote that sets the table.
points.body: The overnight build opens the day, cut before sunrise. Then one sharp opening from a builder a few steps ahead, on what they actually shipped this year.

points.title: 12:30 · Roundtables of around ten.
points.body: Specific, real questions, and long enough to go deep. The format the community asked for, free to drift where the conversation wants to go.

points.title: 16:00 · Hands-on stations, 1:1s, then drinks.
points.body: Partner technology on the table, opt-in and pitch-free, curated introductions between people facing the same problem, and the part where the follow-up gets arranged.

slides.eyebrow: Twelve hours to takeoff · The night before
slides.title: Fifty engineers. One airframe. Twelve hours.
slides.body: The brief is to give it a mind of its own and get it airborne before the doors open. The whole night is filmed and cut before sunrise, and that film opens the festival.

slides.title: Partners do not sponsor the night, they are in it.
slides.body: Their hardware, models and compute go into the build, and their engineers into the room as mentors.

slides.title: Optional, capped, and the part people talk about.

points.title: Real problems, real teams.
points.body: One real challenge on the table, brought by a partner or sourced from the network. No toy briefs, real constraints, real data, real shipping decisions.

points.title: A curated room.
points.body: Around fifty hands-on CTOs and senior engineers, capped on purpose, in mixed teams of four or five paired across companies and stacks.

points.title: It opens the festival.
points.body: The cut plays at kick-off in front of five hundred people, and the teams take the stage for questions. Builders judged by builders.
